problem_statement: A particle moves along the x-axis with acceleration a(t) = (3.0 t - 4.0) m/s^2, where t is in seconds. At time t = 0, the particle is at x(0) = 5.0 m and has velocity v(0) = 2.0 m/s. (a) Determine the velocity as a function of time v(t). (b) Determine the position as a function of time x(t). (c) Find the position of the particle when its velocity reaches a local minimum.
target_quantity: Velocity function v(t), position function x(t), and position at local minimum velocity
governing_principles: a = dv/dt => v(t) = v(0) + int a(t) dt
v = dx/dt => x(t) = x(0) + int v(t) dt
solution_strategy: Integrate acceleration with respect to time using initial velocity as the constant of integration. Integrate velocity to find position. Set dv/dt = a = 0 to identify the stationary point of velocity.

ordered_steps.action_description: Integrate acceleration to obtain velocity function
ordered_steps.justification: Definition of velocity as integral of acceleration.
ordered_steps.calculation_details: Integral of 3 t is 1.5 t^2; integral of -4 is -4 t; adding initial v(0) = 2.0 gives v(t) = 1.5 t^2 - 4.0 t + 2.0 m/s.

ordered_steps.action_description: Integrate velocity to obtain position function
ordered_steps.justification: Definition of position as integral of velocity.
ordered_steps.calculation_details: Integral of 1.5 t^2 is 0.5 t^3; integral of -4 t is -2 t^2; integral of 2 is 2 t; adding initial x(0) = 5.0 gives x(t).

ordered_steps.action_description: Find time of minimum velocity by setting dv/dt = a(t) = 0
ordered_steps.justification: First derivative test: a(t) = dv/dt = 0 with d^2v/dt^2 = da/dt = +3.0 > 0 confirms a local minimum.

ordered_steps.action_description: Substitute t = 4/3 s into position function x(t)

final_answer: v(t) = (1.5 t^2 - 4.0 t + 2.0) m/s; x(t) = (0.5 t^3 - 2.0 t^2 + 2.0 t + 5.0) m; position at minimum velocity is 143/27 m (approx 5.30 m).
sanity_checks: At t = 0: v(0) = 2.0 m/s and x(0) = 5.0 m, which strictly match given initial conditions.
Dimensional check: [1.5 t^2] = [T^-2][T^2] = [1] with pre-factor unit m/s^3 => [L][T]^-1, dimensionally homogeneous.
trap_alerts: Do not use standard kinematic equations v = u + at because acceleration is time-dependent!
